resources.string: Start Pip when the phone starts
Starts Pip after you unlock your phone following a restart.
Automatic start needs “Display over other apps” permission.

Optional. Lets Pip tap, type, and scroll in other apps, such as when you ask him to open Reels or play a playlist, and keep clear of their keyboards. Pip doesn’t record your screen or read password fields. For model-assisted tasks, your request and visible on-screen text may be sent to the AI provider you chose.

The developer does not collect what you tell Pip or ask him to save. The app keeps recent chats and Memory notes on your device. You can review or clear them in Chat history and Pip settings → Memory.

Chat goes directly to your chosen AI provider and may include recent messages and Memory notes. If Pip needs help with a task, he may send your request and visible app text. Your provider’s privacy policy applies.

Passwords in fields Android identifies as password fields and passwords saved in Pip’s login vault are not sent to the API. Don’t paste passwords into chat or leave them visible as plain text in another app while Pip is working.

Accessibility is optional. Leave it off and you can still chat and play with on-screen toys. Pip won’t be able to tap, type, or scroll in other apps for you, so features like Doomscroll and in-app playback controls won’t work. He also won’t be able to see when another app’s keyboard is open.
API verified. Choose the permissions you want to grant. You can finish setup without granting accessibility, and change permissions later in Pip settings → Permissions.

The developer does not collect your chats or Memory notes. Requests go directly to your selected AI provider and may include chat context or visible app text. Password fields and saved vault passwords aren’t sent; don’t put passwords in chat.
Pip defaults to Gemini. You can also use another OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Your API key is stored on this device.
No browser is available to open Google AI Studio.
Pip needs this to appear on your screen.
Lets Pip answer questions about the last app in front without sharing app usage with your chat provider.
Pip can run and listen without notifications. To stop listening, use Talk to Pip in settings. Android may still show the microphone indicator or list Pip among active apps.
Open Android Settings to change this permission.
See Pip’s status, permission checks, and what happened during his last phone job.
Revisit the welcome, API verification, and permissions screens. This won’t clear your chats, Memory, or other settings.
Your current API settings are filled in. Any API changes are saved only when you finish setup.
Optional. Android calls this Notification access. Pip checks active media controls when you ask what’s playing. Pip does not read notification messages or send track metadata to the API.
